title: New York City Public Schools banning AI use through middle school starting this year
source_used: ABC News (full article), checked against the NYC.gov press release of 2 Sep 2026
key_facts: NYC Public Schools confirmed to ABC News a ban on student AI use for the 2026-27 school year, affecting more than half a million students.
The ban covers students from 2-K (early years) through eighth grade; it removes software that uses student-facing AI and bans companion chatbots.
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani says the city will spend the next year studying the impacts of the technology.
The moratorium does not apply to high school students, who get twice-yearly AI literacy classes.
Schools Chancellor Kamar Samuels says the aim is to restore critical thinking and that technology should serve learning.
The White House is pushing teachers to use AI responsibly, and some teachers told ABC they use AI for lesson plans and feedback.
ABC's article and the NYC.gov release are both dated 2 Sep 2026.
quote_evidence: New York City Public Schools is banning more than half a million students from using artificial intelligence for the 2026-2027 academic year, the school district confirmed to ABC News.
The city's AI moratorium does not apply to high school students.
The district said it is implementing the most expansive AI moratorium in the nation, eliminating software that uses student-facing AI and banning companion chatbots.
why_it_matters_hint: The largest US school district is pausing student-facing AI for a year to study its effects.
notes: Google News re-dated the ABC article to 17 Oct 2026; the underlying decision is from 2 Sep 2026.
